en: The steep, zigzag paths of Kennon Road in Benguet act as inclined planes to help vehicles climb the mountain with less effort.
Rural Filipinos use a simple pulley system with a rope and wheel to pull a heavy pail of water from deep wells.
Jeepney drivers apply brakes to increase friction between the rubber tires and the road, stopping the heavy vehicle safely.
Gravity pulls a ripe Guimaras mango straight down to the ground when it detaches from the tree branch.
The black sand beaches of Ilocos Norte contain magnetite, a naturally magnetic mineral that is strongly attracted to magnets.
The Tiwi Geothermal Power Plant in Albay converts thermal energy from underground steam into electrical energy to power local homes.
The white limestone walls of the historic Miag-ao Church in Iloilo reflect light energy from the sun, keeping the interior cooler.
Musicians in Maguindanao strike the brass kulintang gongs, causing the metal to vibrate and produce distinct musical sounds.
The natural hot springs in Los Baños, Laguna, are heated by geothermal energy from magma beneath the Earth's crust.
A Philippine carabao stores chemical energy from eating grass, which its muscles convert into mechanical energy for plowing fields.
Filipino sari-sari store owners use a bottle opener as a lever to pry metal caps off glass soda bottles.
The giant blades of the Bangui wind turbines in Ilocos Norte spin, converting the kinetic energy of moving air into mechanical energy.
